question.prompt: Tell me about a time you had a significant disagreement or conflict with a coworker. How did you handle it, and what was the outcome?
expectedPoints: Structured STAR storytelling (Situation, Task, Action, Result)
Professional conflict resolution focusing on data/product goals rather than personal ego
Demonstrating active listening and empathy for alternative perspectives
Clear measurable outcome and self-reflection on lessons learned
commonMistakes: Blaming coworker or showing unresolved hostility
Lack of reflection or personal growth

transcript: Candidate: There was this junior engineer on my team who was completely incompetent. He was always pushing sloppy code that broke my PRs. I told him multiple times in Slack that he needed to get his act together, but he kept arguing with me and ignoring my comments. Eventually, I realized talking to him was a waste of time, so I just went into his branch, rewrote all of his code myself over the weekend, and merged it so we wouldn't miss our sprint goal. He complained to our manager, but our manager saw that my code worked better, so nothing happened. I proved I was right and we shipped on time.
notes: Severe red flags: abusive language towards colleague, bypassed peer without communication, zero empathy or reflection.
